Hi Alice / Fintegrity SecEng —

Following our onboarding call last week, we want to lock down a short operational plan for private FQDN ownership and TLS termination for the embedded Redwood Private deployment inside your VPC. Key things we need to confirm so we can finalize the deployment runbook: 

- The canonical private FQDN you want Redwood to serve (you mentioned *.redwood-fin.trust but we need exact hostnames for certs).
- Who will own DNS zone attestations (NS/CNAME delegation vs stub-zone) and whether your infra team can allow a short-lived DNS proof (TXT / CNAME) during onboarding.
- Where TLS terminates: customer-managed TLS at their edge, or Redwood-managed TLS proxy inside the VPC (we support both; each has different cert rotation responsibilities).
- KMS / HSM integration expectations if you need customer-managed keys for certs.

Attachments: tls-routing-diagram.v1.png (proposed split-termination patterns), csr-template-fin.json (CSR template we use for private FQDNs).

Proposed immediate next steps: small 30-minute sync with your infra/security folks to agree on which termination model and the DNS proof flow. Can you share two 30-minute windows tomorrow or Monday?

Thanks —

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary. From Fintegrity's side:

- Canonical hosts: api.redwood-fin.internal and auth.redwood-fin.internal. We will own the top-level private zone redwood-fin.internal in our VPC resolver.
- DNS proof: we can create a short-lived TXT record for attestations but prefer not to give zone delegation. Prefer pattern where Redwood provides a challenge value we place as TXT and then remove after validation.
- TLS termination: security prefers customer-managed termination at our edge (we have an ingress proxy) for compliance, but we understand the benefit of a Redwood-managed TLS proxy inside the VPC for simplified cert rotation. We need to evaluate both for SLA and key custody.
- KMS: For compliance reasons we need keys in our KMS; we would like Redwood to support issuing certs signed by our CA (bring-your-own-CA) or accept a CSR we generate that is signed by our internal CA.

Before the sync, we also need an inventory of: OCSP/CRL endpoints you expect Redwood to hit (if any), any outbound egress IP ranges for OCSP/CRL/KMS calls, and the CSR format you require. Can you include those in the diagram or as a short checklist?

Availability: Friday 6/19 10:00–11:00 ET or Monday 6/22 09:00–10:00 ET.

Best,

Alice — thanks for the detail and for the availability. I've annotated the attached tls-routing-diagram.v1.png with two recommended patterns and the operational responsibilities for each:

Pattern A — Customer-edge termination (preferred for compliance):
- Fintegrity manages the full TLS termination at your ingress proxy.
- Redwood will provide CSR templates; you sign with your CA and upload certs + chain to our private runtime via the admin console or an encrypted S3 transfer.
- Cert rotation: Fintegrity rotates certs on your ingress; Redwood will accept new certs and reload without downtime.
- DNS proof: short-lived TXT validation that you control (you create TXT containing our challenge), then we validate and delete locally. No zone delegation required.

Pattern B — Redwood in-VPC termination (operational simplicity):
- Redwood runs a small TLS proxy inside your VPC (customer-hosted templates) and either uses Redwood-managed certs or BYO-CA via CSR.
- Cert rotation handled by Redwood's cert manager; finite window for key custody can be negotiated (we support HSM integration where customer keys never leave your KMS via signing‑as-a-service).
- DNS flow uses the same TXT challenge pattern or a temporary CNAME proof if you prefer programmatic automation.

For Pattern A we've noted the checklist you asked for: OCSP/CRL endpoints — Redwood will validate OCSP on behalf of the runtime but we can disable stapling if you prefer (please confirm). Outbound egress: 52.23.178.0/24, 54.142.12.0/24 (these are our control-plane IPs for cert validation and orchestration; we can place them in a smaller set if needed). CSR format: see attached csr-template-fin.json (we also support PKCS#10).

I'll take the sync on Monday 6/22 09:00 ET. Jordan/Marissa — can you lock the calendar and invite Fintegrity's infra eng?

Kimberly Park

Great — thanks all. Calendar invite sent for Mon 2026-06-22 09:00 ET (30m). A couple operational bullets from the deployment side so we have alignment before the call: 

- Pre-call deliverables from Fintegrity: list of exact hostname(s) (api/auth), confirmation of TXT proof lifecycle policy (how long records can persist), and the KMS model (BYO-CA vs Redwood-signed with key escrow).
- Pre-call deliverables from Redwood: final diagram (I've versioned tls-routing-diagram.v1.png -> v1.1 and added the OCSP egress ranges), a short runbook stub for Pattern A/B we can walk through on the call, and a draft canary rollout plan for cert swaps (5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2-hour windows).
- Compliance ask: if Fintegrity requires HSM key signing in your KMS, bring the KMS admin to the call so we can map out signing workflow and audit logging expectations (we will need a short PO to enable BYO-CA support in the private runtime).

I linked the JIRA ticket INF-9123 that will track the deployment tasks and HubSpot deal HS-5841 for contractual items. Post-call we'll convert agreed responsibilities into a 1-page ownership matrix and an ACL for the zone-attestation TXT lifecycle.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.
